newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina may post small trade gap in '96-official.
newsitem.headline: Argentina may post small trade gap in '96-official.

text.p: Argentina may finish 1996 with a "small" trade deficit or a balanced trade account after a surplus of $900 million in 1995, said Carlos Rodriguez, chief aide to economy minister Roque Fernandez.

"It won't surprise me if this year ends with a balance or a small trade deficit. Until now there has been a rebound in the economy and the arrival of capital has to generate a trade deficit," Rodriguez told reporters. He predicted a deficit in the fourth quarter, which "traditionally happens."
Rodriguez's comments were the first hint Argentina's trade account could end in deficit this year.
Until now, the Economy Ministry had predicted a balanced trade standing for 1996.
In the first eight months of the year, there was a trade surplus of $636 million with exports at $15.838 billion and imports at $15.202 billion.

Separately, Rodriguez said "if gross domestic product in the fourth quarter grows at the same rate as in the second and third, its likely growth will be three percent for the year. We are plainly seeing a rebound in economic activity."

The Economy Ministry said Wednesday preliminary figures for the Argentine economy showed growth of 6.6 percent in the third quarter of this year over the same quarter a year ago. The data exceeded economists' expectations for growth of 5.4 percent.

Fixed gross investment increased 17 percent in the third quarter. Additionally, bank lending grew 9.1 percent compared with the same quarter a year earlier while bank deposits were 18.6 percent higher.
"The growth in deposits shows a rise in confidence, and higher confidence ultimately has to lead to a fall in country risk," said Rodriguez.

"If I see that deposits rise, interest rates will fall," predicted the official. He added that a rise of 40 percent in the MerVal stock index in October over its year-ago level shows the economy has solid prospects.
